extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and diplomatic/legal observers interested in UN Security Council procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive guidance and arguments about whether and when the UN Security Council must or may remove items from its agenda after parties to a dispute request withdrawal, and about the Council's duty and powers in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter silence on mandatory removal from agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: “cannot find anywhere in the Charter anything which says that the Council must, if two parties to a dispute demand it, remove a matter from its agenda” — the Charter does not explicitly provide for mandatory removal of an item at the parties' request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Charter is silent on this point, this procedural question must be resolved by interpretation and practice; the Secretary‑General’s paper and the Committee of Experts' report are relied on to clarify the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case adjudication / common-sense discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: “we have a Council which should be guided to a certain extent by common sense, and it seems to me each case should be considered on its merits.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid laying down a single general rule governing all situations; rather assess each dispute’s factual and legal context before deciding whether to keep it on the agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: State's right to withdraw a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: “it is very unwise and even a dangerous doctrine to maintain that a country has no right to withdraw a complaint from this Council.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respecting a state's right to withdraw encourages states — especially smaller ones — to bring disputes to the Council; denying withdrawal could discourage recourse to the Council and politicize complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of agreement/withdrawal: closure of dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: “when two parties reach an agreement and notify us… the only conclusions we can draw… is that there is no more dispute and that therefore the case is closed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notified settlement and subsequent withdrawal of the complaint is normally taken as terminating the dispute, absent indications that the settlement leaves unresolved issues of international concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council may remain seized if agreement creates new international friction
rubrics_metrics.description: “the Security Council may remain seized of a dispute even after the parties' withdrawal… if the agreement is not satisfactory and which may lead to international friction or give rise to a new dispute.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a settlement or its implementation creates a continuing or new situation of international concern, the Council may legitimately continue to treat the matter as before it and take further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: another member must present new situation
rubrics_metrics.description: “some member of the Council must take upon himself the responsibility and present the case to the Council in its new form as a situation which leads to international friction.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where parties have withdrawn complaints but a new or continuing situation exists, a member must formally bring that transformed situation to the Council (e.g., invoke Article 34) as a separate act for Council consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure independent of Article 34 measures
rubrics_metrics.description: “the decision by which the Security Council is seized of a question may be independent of any measures taken under Article 34.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council seizure of a matter can arise through means other than preliminary steps under Article 34; this broader reading supports the Council's inherent powers to address threats to peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council duty to supervise until settlement implemented
rubrics_metrics.description: “the Council is not a passive body… it is the right but even the duty to supervise a case once it is placed before the Council until settlement is carried out.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a case is before the Council, it may have an obligation to monitor implementation and ensure that agreed remedies are effected before concluding its responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to act in conformity with justice and international law
rubrics_metrics.description: “the Security Council shall act in conformity with the principles of Justice and international law.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In discharging its duties — including decisions about retention or removal of items — the Council must respect legal principles and fairness, a matter of particular importance to smaller states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council determines its agenda; agenda rests with the Council
rubrics_metrics.description: “the matter of an agenda really rests with the Council once it has come before the attention of the Council… it is a matter for the Council to decide what should or should not remain on its agenda.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of whether an item remains on the Council’s agenda is a Council prerogative and not automatically controlled by the wishes of the disputing parties.
